Subject: Confirmation of derivative handling, geo-routing, and model-improvement opt-out

Hi Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare procurement paperwork, our legal team needs a short note from Redwood confirming two operational points so we can close the DPA: 

1) No-model-improvement / No-training: VitalBridge requires that interactions and prompt/response data from our tenant be excluded from any model improvement pipelines (no adaptive training, no permanent dataset ingestion). We understand Redwood uses ephemeral KV caches and may keep telemetry for ops — acceptable as long as it is not used for training.

2) Output / Prompt Ownership & Derivatives: We require an explicit statement that customer prompts and generated outputs are licensed back to the customer for their internal use and that Redwood does not assert ownership over customer-provided prompts or derivations. (Export/transfer exceptions for analytics are OK if redacted.)

3) Geo-routing / Subprocessor residency: Because VitalBridge is US-only for patient data, we need confirmation that processing for their tenant can be pinned to US regions and that any subprocessors that would access raw interactions are US-based. If non-US subprocessors are required, please list them and describe residency/fallback options.

We attached a simple DPA redline and an evidence matrix that lists the operational protections we expect. Can you confirm in writing and, if possible, provide the short wording VitalBridge's legal team should include in the contract (1–2 sentences per item)?

Attachments: VB_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (redline), vitalbridge_evidence_matrix.xlsx

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants this in the next 72 hours.

Best,
Clara West
Senior Counsel, VitalBridge Health
clara.west@vitalbridgehealth.com

--

Thanks for the ping, Jonas. I reviewed VitalBridge's redline and sketched proposed language below. I focused on concise, contract-friendly statements that map to operational controls we can reasonably commit to. Please review and call out anything you think is operationally infeasible.

Proposed clauses (short form):

1) No-Training: "Redwood will not use Customer-provided prompts, conversations, or generated outputs from the Customer's tenant for model training, model updates, or model improvement. Customer interaction data may be retained for operational monitoring and debugging in accordance with the Agreement, but such telemetry will not be incorporated into model training datasets."

2) Prompt/Output License: "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer-provided prompts and in the outputs generated by Redwood for Customer requests. Redwood hereby grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use and exploit such outputs for its business purposes, without Redwood asserting ownership of Customer prompts or derived outputs."

3) Geo-routing & Subprocessors: "Redwood will route processing for Customer interactions to infrastructure located in the United States (us-east-1 / us-west-2) for the Customer's tenant. Redwood will restrict access to raw interaction content to subprocessors and personnel that are contractually bound to the same residency and non-training commitments. A non-exhaustive list of subprocessors that may access raw interactions is: [list to be provided]. Should Redwood need to engage a non-US subprocessor, Redwood will provide prior notice and an appropriate mitigation plan (e.g., onshore fallback, data minimization, contractual safeguards)."

Operational notes / clarifications needed: 
- We should explicitly permit ephemeral caching (KV caches) for latency but exclude persistent dataset ingestion. Wording above references monitoring vs training but let's keep the distinction clear in definitions.
- If VitalBridge requires an onshore-only subprocessor list up front, that may trigger additional procurement work; we should offer to provide a current list with defined residency and escalation path.
- I recommend we attach the evidence matrix VitalBridge provided and propose a DocuSign addendum that includes the three short clauses. Marissa, can ops provide a current list of subprocessors that would touch raw interactions for a typical tenant? David, please confirm telemetry retention windows and whether logs are stored in a way we can guarantee non-training status (e.g., redaction, access controls).

If this language looks good, we can send it back to Clara with the redline applied and propose a DocuSign route for a DPA addendum.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--

Hi Clara —

Appreciate the clear matrix and timeline. Kimberly drafted short clauses that map to operational commitments; Marissa and David have reviewed operations feasibility and confirmed we can comply with the statements below. Please see the concise wording we propose for insertion into the DPA addendum (we've kept each item to one sentence per your ask):

1) No-Training: "Redwood will not use Customer-provided prompts, conversations, or generated outputs from the Customer's tenant for model training, model updates, or model improvement. Activity may be retained for operational monitoring and debugging, but such telemetry will not be used in training datasets."

2) Prompt/Output License: "Customer retains all rights to Customer-provided prompts and outputs generated for the Customer; Redwood does not claim ownership of those prompts or derived outputs and grants Customer a perpetual, royalty-free license to use them."

3) Geo-routing & Subprocessors: "Redwood will route processing for Customer interactions to infrastructure located in the United States (us-east-1 / us-west-2) for the Customer tenancy. Redwood will restrict access to raw interaction content to subprocessors contractually bound to the same residency and non-training commitments; Redwood will notify Customer prior to engaging any non-US subprocessor and propose mitigation steps as needed."

Attachments: I have uploaded a revised DPA redline that inserts the language above (VB_DPA_redline_v2.pdf) and the evidence matrix with operational notes. For transparency, Marissa will share a current subprocessor snapshot and David will share the telemetry retention policy excerpt.

Next steps: if this wording is acceptable to VitalBridge, we can generate a DocuSign DPA addendum (link to follow) and include the evidence matrix as an appendix. If you prefer alternate phrasing for any clause, tell us which line to change and we'll update the redline.
